gen-gf-offside-gf-kedebideri: Expressive from the first glance, Offside tracks its letters wide and leaves its curves unfinished, never leaning on weight for emphasis. Offside makes statements; Kedebideri, rounded and open, simply reads.
gen-gf-offside-gf-khula: Wide, level, unshaded: Offside keeps a constant stroke weight throughout and never quite closes its curves. Khula takes over below with a tall midsection and curves that hold their mouths open too.
gen-gf-offside-gf-krub: Krub reads contemporary, with a pronounced x-height and curves that lift away before the loop closes. Offside above it stays unshaded and widely spaced, so the two never compete.
gen-gf-offside-gf-kufam: Offside spaces its letters wide and never fully closes a curve. Kufam draws a single track width, like neon tubing, with generously open curves and bodies that crowd out its ascenders.
gen-gf-offside-gf-lexend: Curves that refuse to close give Offside its edge. Lexend stretches its lowercase large and keeps every curve open, with thickness that holds around the bends, so whole paragraphs move along smoothly.
gen-gf-offside-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca reads clean and approachable, drawing a plain unshaded line whose terminals stop short instead of curling back in. Offside handles the loud moments; this one handles the quiet ones.
gen-gf-offside-gf-liter: Commanding, Offside spaces its letters wide and leaves curves open. Liter carries the pair with vertical presence: a lowercase with no stroke contrast and wide mouths on its round forms.
gen-gf-offside-gf-mada: Wire-bent s curves that never thin define Offside. Offside is best at commanding attention with that level line, while Mada does its work with a towering midzone and curves left open.
gen-gf-offside-gf-martel-sans: Thread-plain, wide-set, unhurried: Offside draws strokes as simple as a stitched outline. And the strongest thing here is Martel Sans, whose high mean line and generous curve openings lift every word.
gen-gf-offside-gf-matangi: Below, the text reads hefty and contemporary, strokes like twine pressed flat. Matangi and Offside share a habit of leaving curves open, and that shared openness is the pair's real strength.
